bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: Allocate evaluation contexts on a stack of their own instead of the C stack

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
eval(), R_forceAndCall() and bcEval_loop() each keep an RCNTXT in their stack frame for the builtin-call context, which is set up only while profiling or (in the first two) for foreign calls such as .Call(). One such frame is held per level whenever R code recurses through C: do.call(), lapply(), eval(), S3 dispatch.

Reproducible example: builtin-context-stack-repro.R, attached, prints the depth reached before "C stack usage is too close to the limit". With an 8 MB stack on macOS arm64 (r90883, clang) it is 1959 through do.call(), 1936 through lapply() and 1750 through eval(); with the patch 2833, 2770 and 2418.

Proposed patch: attached as builtin-context-helper.diff, against r90883. It moves the context, with the begincontext()/endcontext() sequence, into one helper shared by the three callers and kept out of line with R_NOINLINE (the macro from the patch in bug 19315; the Defn.h hunk is identical). The three frames shrink from 592, 528 and 1712 bytes to 160, 112 and 1328; when a context is created is unchanged.

make check passes, and tracebacks and error calls from foreign calls are as before. The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/484, where CI results can be seen.

Created attachment 4062
patch: move the builtin-call context into a shared out-of-line helper; add R_NOINLINE

Created attachment 4064
patch: allocate builtin-call contexts on the node stack (applies on top of attachment 4062)

A possible further step, on top of attachment 4062: builtin-context-pool.diff, attached, allocates the builtin context on the byte code node stack, as is done for inlined closure calls, instead of in the helper's frame. That frame shrinks from 512 bytes to 80, and with an 8 MB stack, recursion through a foreign call from interpreted code or forceAndCall(), or through a builtin call while profiling, gets 7 to 12% deeper. There is no speed benefit.

It is a trade-off, though: each active context takes 448 bytes of node stack, so with a 64 MB C stack the node stack runs out first and the same recursion gets shallower (from 14531 to 6658 levels while profiling; builtin-context-pool-repro.R, attached).

make check passes. Patch also at https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/485.

comments.text: I've thought about converting more contexts to use the node stack but the code complication didn't seem warranted. Doing so would be more appealing if the code base could be simplified at the same time, e.g. by getting rid of all C-stack-allocated contexts and replacing them by heap allocated ones, either on the node-stack or by `R_alloc()` (maybe a specifically tuned version).

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
Created attachment 4101
patch: allocate all contexts on a stack of their own (against r90926)

Thanks Luke -- I've put together a patch. It moves every context, including the byte code interpreter's, to a stack of its own: one array of 16384 contexts, allocated at startup and released in LIFO order.

The patch touches many files, but most of it is mechanical: `begincontext()` now allocates and returns the context, and call sites use it or the `simplecontext()` and `codecontext()` shorthands. The substantive changes are in `context.c` (the stack) and `eval.c` (byte code inline calls and loops, and the overflow check).

With an 8 MB stack, recursion through C goes 1.7 to 1.9 times deeper, compiled recursion 2.3 times. Overflow raises a catchable `contextStackOverflowError`; only setups that already raise `options(expressions)` and `--max-ppsize` (or profile) on a large C stack stop earlier.

Patch also at https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/506.
